meta.title: Acquisition model: default assumptions, benchmarks and presets
meta.author: Syed Rahman
meta.method: Benchmarks reuse source entries already cited in the Punctual Pros, CET, Frontline and Thomas Scientific growth plans and the sponsor precedents. Portfolio presets take the midpoints of each company's filings estimate table. Add-on presets read the target screens at load time and apply the sector margin below. Rows marked as assumptions have no market source.
caveats: Presets are estimates from public filings, not BSP's actual terms.
Market multiples are averages; any single deal can differ widely.
Press-reported exit multiples (Sila, Champions) are estimates from people familiar with the deals.

inputs.label: Revenue today
inputs.gloss: Annual sales of the company being bought.

inputs.label: EBITDA margin
inputs.gloss: Profit before interest, tax and depreciation, as a share of revenue.

inputs.label: Entry multiple
inputs.gloss: Price paid, as a multiple of EBITDA.

inputs.label: Debt at entry
inputs.gloss: Borrowing, as a multiple of EBITDA.

inputs.label: Interest rate
inputs.gloss: Annual interest on the debt.

inputs.label: Revenue growth
inputs.gloss: Organic growth, before add-ons.

inputs.label: Margin change
inputs.gloss: How much the EBITDA margin moves each year.

inputs.label: Exit year
inputs.gloss: How long the fund owns the company.

inputs.label: Exit multiple
inputs.gloss: Sale price, as a multiple of EBITDA in the exit year.

inputs.label: Add-on EBITDA bought
inputs.gloss: EBITDA of the smaller companies bought each year until exit.

inputs.label: Add-on multiple
inputs.gloss: Price paid for add-ons, as a multiple of their EBITDA.

inputs.label: Add-ons paid with debt
inputs.gloss: Share of each add-on price that is borrowed; the rest is new equity.

inputs.label: Cash conversion
inputs.gloss: EBITDA left after tax, capital spending and working capital, before interest.

inputs.label: Deal fees
inputs.gloss: Bankers, lawyers and financing costs at entry.

inputs.label: Tax rate
inputs.gloss: Tax on operating profit.

inputs.label: Depreciation
inputs.gloss: Wear on equipment and vehicles, a non-cash cost.

inputs.label: Capital spending
inputs.gloss: Trucks, tools, systems and buildings.

inputs.label: Working capital
inputs.gloss: Cash tied up in receivables and stock as sales grow.

inputs.label: Discount rate (WACC)
inputs.gloss: The return investors and lenders require, blended.

inputs.label: Long-run growth
inputs.gloss: Growth after year 5, forever.

inputs.label: Year-5 sale multiple
inputs.gloss: Cross-check: value in year 5 as a multiple of EBITDA.

inputs.label: Net debt today
inputs.gloss: Debt minus cash; subtracted to get the value of the shares.

inputs.label: Company EBITDA
inputs.gloss: EBITDA of the company that does the buying.

inputs.label: Company multiple paid
inputs.gloss: Price paid for that company, as a multiple of EBITDA.

inputs.label: Number of add-ons
inputs.gloss: Smaller companies bought and merged in.

inputs.label: EBITDA per add-on
inputs.gloss: Typical size of each add-on.

inputs.label: Add-on multiple paid
inputs.gloss: Smaller companies usually sell for less.

inputs.label: Exit multiple
inputs.gloss: Sale price of the combined company, as a multiple of EBITDA.

inputs.label: Integration cost
inputs.gloss: One-off cost to merge systems, brands and teams.

inputs.label: Synergies
inputs.gloss: Extra EBITDA from shared buying, dispatch and back office.

items.label: Typical lower-middle-market deal
items.summary: A $50M-revenue services company bought at the GF Data average.

basis.em: GF Data Q2 2026: 7.0x average for initial buyouts.
basis.ir: GF Data Q2 2026: senior debt priced at 7.8%.
basis.am: GF Data: deals under $25M of value average 6.3 to 6.9x.
basis.xm: Equal to the 7.0x entry multiple: no multiple expansion assumed. The returns view shows the result with +2.0x as an option.

items.label: Punctual Pros
items.summary: Home services in Pennsylvania and New Jersey; FY2025 size from public estimates ($22M revenue, $2.6M EBITDA).

basis.rev: FY2025 pro forma revenue about $22M (range $16M to $28M), from franchise disclosures and headcount; the nationwide plan grows this to an October 2026 run-rate of about $24M.
basis.mg: Adjusted EBITDA about $2.6M for FY2025 after franchise royalties (8 to 14% margin); about $2.9M on the October 2026 run-rate.
basis.em: Entry value about $18M to $30M, 7 to 10x estimated EBITDA.
basis.lev: Senior debt about $10M to $18M, 4 to 5.5x EBITDA.
basis.gr: 2025 same-store sales rose 8.4% to 14.3% across the three brands.
basis.ae: About one small tuck-in a year, the size of the Horvath deal.
basis.ra: Screened Punctual Pros targets have about $6M to $15M of revenue.

items.note: Size from public estimates (est.); deal terms use the market benchmarks, so the return is forward-looking for a deal of this size, not a verdict on the original entry price.

items.label: CET
items.summary: Commercial electrical in New England, pro forma with NuWave and Horton; filings-based estimates.

basis.rev: Pro forma with NuWave and Horton: $65M to $100M of revenue (midpoint about $82M), the estimate the Command Center shows.
basis.mg: Pro forma EBITDA $6M to $11M (about $8.5M), roughly a 10% margin, bracketed by Limbach and IES.
basis.em: Entry value about $35M to $75M, 9 to 12x EBITDA.
basis.lev: 3.5 to 5.5x lower-middle-market leverage; lender not disclosed.
basis.gr: Listed electrical peers grew 16.8% a year (median); 10% assumed.
basis.xm: Equal to the entry multiple: no re-rating assumed.
basis.ae: Horton-sized add-ons ($25M to $40M revenue) every 18 to 24 months.

items.note: Size from public estimates (est.); deal terms use the market benchmarks, so the return is forward-looking for a deal of this size, not a verdict on the original entry price.

items.label: BPI

basis.rev: FY2025 net revenue $85M to $125M (midpoint about $105M), the estimate the Command Center shows.
basis.mg: FY2025 adjusted EBITDA $17M to $28M (about $22.5M), 18 to 24% of net revenue, below listed peers at 24 to 33%.

basis.lev: 3.5 to 5.0x; the credit agreement followed the close by seven months.
basis.gr: Listed agency peers grew 2.8% a year (median).

items.label: Fair Harbor
items.summary: Consumer apparel brand, size at entry (2021); priced on revenue, so EBITDA multiples run high.

basis.rev: 2021 revenue $30M to $40M before the BSP deal.
basis.mg: Assumed; listed apparel peers earn 6 to 18%.
basis.em: Entry value $40M to $90M, about 1.9x revenue, so about 15.5x a 12% margin.
basis.lev: No term loan found; at most a small inventory credit line.
basis.gr: Listed apparel peers grew 1.0% a year (median); 5% assumed for a younger brand.
basis.xm: Assumed: a mature brand is usually worth less per dollar of EBITDA.

items.note: Size from public estimates (est.); deal terms use the market benchmarks, so the return is forward-looking for a deal of this size, not a verdict on the original entry price.

items.label: Analyst assumptions without a market source

items.cc: Half of EBITDA reaches debt repayment after tax, capital spending and working capital.
items.fee: 3% of price for bankers, lawyers and financing.
items.ad: Half of each add-on paid with debt, half with new fund equity.
items.tax: 25% combined federal and state rate on operating profit.
items.wacc: 12% blended required return for a lower-middle-market company.
items.tg: 3% long-run growth, about the rate of nominal GDP.
items.ic: $0.3M per add-on to merge systems, brands and teams.
items.syn: 10% of add-on EBITDA from shared purchasing and dispatch.
items.hurdle: 20% annual return (2.5x money multiple) used to colour the sensitivity tables.
